rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 4 "The model has read the field", line 223: "The weights hold the written record: the setup posts, the plan-file templates, the verifier write-ups, the reversals." The first three list items map cleanly onto chunks 2-3, which just spent two slides establishing reference-artefact / plan.md / external-verifier — "setup posts", "plan-file templates" and "verifier write-ups" all read as "writing about the thing we just named." "The reversals" does not map onto anything: grepped the body above the maintainer cut for "reversal" — one hit, this line, no other occurrence anywhere before or after it in the student-facing text. This is not merely under-specified (the compendium's "vague with full history" example, "a system like this", at least narrows to a shortlist) — a cold reader has zero candidates to narrow to. The backing block (student-invisible) supplies the referent via amp-handoff/amp-neo (a vendor's compaction-vs-handoff reversal), but that pairing never surfaces in the body, so nothing in-file resolves it. Harm check: this module's own delivery contract (learn-from-the-test.md maintainer block, "Dense-slides note") states the bullets ARE the evidence with no trainer narration filling gaps — an unexplained, specific-sounding definite noun phrase mid-list either stalls a listener or gets silently dropped, which undercuts the exact claim ("the weights hold the written record") the bullet exists to evidence. The harm is present, and naming what kind of reversal (or cutting the item back to the three that already map) costs the artefact nothing.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name what reversal you mean (e.g. "the reversals when a team's own setup posts contradict each other"), or drop the fourth list item and let the three that already map stand alone.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Bold count per chunk (grepped '\*\*' against the body): chunk1=1 ("A check is a position fix"), chunk2=2 ("Reference artefact" / "plan.md" — pre-existing since before this file's last audit, covered by this file's own maintainer accept-note citing the rule's "one handle per law" consolidation-slide exception), chunk3=1 ("External verifier"), chunk4=1 ("candidates"), chunk5=1 ("A prediction is not a measurement."), chunk6=1 ("The engineer decides"), chunk7=1 ("hook"), chunk8=1 ("Must happen goes in a hook"). All within the ≤1-per-slide budget except chunk2's pre-existing, already-accepted exception. Closest call, and new since this file's last slides pass: chunk5's "A prediction is not a measurement." is a full six-word declarative sentence bolded whole, which a literal read of "never a whole lead sentence" would catch. But it functions as one of three parallel epigrammatic "laws" this file coins as its device across the chart and theory slides — chunk1's "A check is a position fix" (same length, already accepted) and chunk6's "The engineer decides" (shorter, same shape) are its siblings — each is the sole bold on its slide and IS the governing claim of its bullet, not a lead-in to elaboration below it, matching rule 9's own "named laws" category. Harm check: the rule exists to stop every-bullet-bolded monoculture that dilutes which bold is a real handle; here exactly one law is bolded per slide against otherwise-plain bullets, so the signal the rule protects stays intact. Not filing a REVISE.
